name: Plyometric Jump Lunge
description: The plyometric jump lunge combines a reverse lunge with a vertical jump, in which the athlete lunges down and then explosively jumps from the lunge position, landing softly back into the same lunge before repeating. Unlike the split jump, the athlete does not switch legs mid-air, making it a true unilateral explosive exercise per leg. It develops single-leg explosive power and lunge-pattern deceleration strength, and is an effective conditioning tool for lower body power endurance.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright with feet together. Step one foot back into a reverse lunge to begin.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Non-slip surface with adequate overhead clearance.
steps: Step 1: Step into a reverse lunge with the right foot back, lowering until both knees are near 90 degrees.
Step 2: Drive off the front (left) foot explosively, extending fully through the hip and knee to jump upward.
Step 3: Land softly back in the same lunge position and absorb through the front leg.
Step 4: Complete all reps on one leg before switching.
Step 5: Perform equal reps on each side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at takeoff. Inhale as you descend into the lunge.
common_mistakes: Landing with the front knee caving inward
Insufficient depth — the rear knee should approach the floor
Using the rear leg to push off — the front leg does the work
safety_considerations: High demand on the front knee — ensure solid lunge mechanics before adding the jump.
Progress from walking lunges and reverse lunges before this variation.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full lunge depth — rear knee approaching the floor. Full extension at takeoff.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 6–10 explosive reps per leg for power. Up to 15 for conditioning.
coaching_cues: Drive off the front foot — not the back
Front knee over the toes at all times
